method: Blind textual re-derivation. (1) `git rev-parse HEAD` on the read-only tree. (2) grep for formal-conjectures URLs / 40-hex ids in the named files to find the project's own pins. (3) curl the upstream file from raw.githubusercontent.com at each cited pin and at `main`, plus the GitHub API commit record of `main`, the file's commit history, the commit records of both pins, the Millenium directory listing, and the upstream notation source files (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/*.lean) and FormalConjecturesUtil.lean at the 8bf45ed7 pin; sha256 + byte count recorded for every fetch; every file saved under writeup/data/arc7/k2/r2/agent_4_upstream/. (4) `diff` upstream vs ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.lean, and challenge vs NavierStokes/ComparatorDefinitions.lean. (5) Python per-declaration extraction (docstring / attribute lines / code block from keyword to next blank line) for every declaration the two theorems depend on, compared raw and whitespace-collapsed against upstream, for the challenge file, the definitions file, and the solution file's theorem statements. (6) Region check: the whole definitional region and the (C)/(D) theorem region compared byte-for-byte after removing exactly the enumerated attribute/notation-scope edits. No lake/lean run; nothing written under the tree.

euler_note: Upstream formal-conjectures has NO Euler file (Millenium directory at main: BSD, NavierStokes, Poincare, PvsNP, RiemannHypothesis). ComparatorChallenges/Euler.lean (cites `main`, unpinned) and Euler/SolutionDefinitions.lean (cites 8323e878) are project-authored specialisations of the upstream Navier–Stokes definitions: n fixed to 3, viscosity and force removed (`euler : ... = -gradient (p · t) x`), `Function.uncurry` spelled out instead of `↿`, docstrings rewritten, helper lemmas dropped, and Euler.lean adds an entirely new Sobolev-class solution concept and theorem `exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity` with no upstream counterpart. No byte-identity claim is possible for Euler and the project does not make one ('Adapted from'); SolutionDefinitions.lean's 'reproduce the independent reference exactly' refers to the project's own Euler challenge file, not to upstream. Out of scope for the gate, which names only the two Navier–Stokes theorems.
